summary: New US data shows nearly 880,000 AI chips were approved for Chinese firms, while Tencent and Alibaba say home-grown chips will soften tighter US rules.
body: A US House committee released records on Thursday showing the Commerce Department approved about 879,000 advanced Nvidia and AMD AI chips for Chinese companies between December 2025 and May 2026, out of 3.4 million requested. Tencent was approved for 150,000, Alibaba 75,000 and Baidu 43,000.[^1][^3] It is unclear how many were actually shipped.[^1] A former US official said more than 30% went to firms the Pentagon lists as linked to China's military; Nvidia says the sales had strict conditions and it has since stopped shipping its H200 chip to China.[^1]

This week US rules also tightened: licences are now needed for advanced chips sent to data centres in Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil, a route Chinese firms used to rent computing power.[^2][^3] On their earnings calls, Tencent and Alibaba said Chinese-made chips can carry much of their cloud work. Tencent president Martin Lau said training its next AI model will take longer and that the rules set "everyone back in China", but will speed up the country's own chip industry.[^2]

The two companies are still growing. Alibaba's AI and cloud revenue rose 53% in the latest quarter, and Tencent's spending on equipment rose more than sixfold.[^2] Alibaba also faces a shareholder lawsuit alleging it hid ties to a Singapore cloud firm suspected of moving restricted chips into China, which that firm denies.[^2] My read: each new US limit pushes China's tech giants further toward their own chips, even at the cost of slower AI progress for now.
differences: Nvidia says its approved China sales were limited and conditional; critics in Washington question whether there was a serious security review.[^1] Tencent says the new rules will slow its AI work; Alibaba says its own chip progress is ahead of plan.[^2]

reads.title: Alibaba and Tencent put their faith in Chinese chips as U.S. curbs threatens to slow down their AI development
reads.summary: How China's two biggest tech firms plan to keep their AI and cloud businesses growing under new US chip rules, and what they admit it will cost.
